exposure: traditional supine position during the second stage of labor
Intervention group (predefined postural changes guided by a physiotherapist)
Intervention of a physiotherapist during the second stage of labor
intervention of a multidisciplinary nursing team including a physiotherapist during the second stage of labor
Traditional supine position during the second stage of labor
predefined postural changes during the passive phase of the second stage of labor under the guidance of the attending physiotherapist
outcome: duration of the second stage of labor
cohort: 150 women undergoing labor with epidural analgesia after a normal gestation.
finding: The intervention of a physiotherapist during the second stage of labor significantly improved obstetric outcomes, leading to more eutocic deliveries, fewer instrumental deliveries and cesarean sections, a shorter second stage of labor, and fewer episiotomies.
mod_finding: The intervention group had significantly fewer instrumental deliveries and cesarean sections compared to the control group.
